items.title: BHP committed to net zero by 2050. Leaked documents show it could be out of reach
items.description: The mining giant's delay in the rollout of renewable energy and a fleet of electric trucks and trains in the Pilbara has raised doubts inside the company about it meeting its ambitious climate goal.

items.title: Labor to ignore call for pause on CGT changes
items.description: The government is pushing ahead with capital gains tax changes while consulting on limited carve-outs.

items.title: Inside Xi's banquet diplomacy and why Albanese missed out on Peking duck
items.description: Xi Jinping has learned that every ingredient placed on a state table is a word in a diplomatic sentence.

items.title: Iran says 'no tolls' on Strait of Hormuz, but warns everything has a cost
items.description: While on assignment inside Iran, our reporter asked a foreign ministry official about the regime's plan for the Strait of Hormuz. The spokesperson responded that "there is no toll" but also signalled crossing the strait would not be entirely free.

items.title: 'Intolerable': When $768m bridge was being designed, engineers raised a red flag
items.description: There are fresh concerns over the structural integrity of Hobart's new Bridgewater Bridge, which one expert who worked on the project suggested could eventually lead to a need to reduce traffic flow or speed limits.

items.title: Missing man's ex-girlfriend feared being 'jumped'
items.description: The former girlfriend of missing Queensland man Jack McLennan says she held fears for her safety because of rumours surrounding his disappearance.

items.title: Live: Save the Children slams 'disappointing' debate over returning IS-linked families
items.description: Save the Children has welcomed the news that a group of Australian children and their mothers, who have been linked to Islamic State militants, could return home within days. Follow live.

items.title: After losing her 3yo daughter, one mum says MDMA therapy saved her life
items.description: Jess Yugovich is among the Australians trying MDMA-assisted psychotherapy after being diagnosed with PTSD, as highly regulated facilities process the drug for therapeutic use.

items.title: Bringing them Home inaction a 'woeful failure', ex-commissioner says
items.description: Mick Dodson heard "soul-destroying" testimony from more than 500 First Nations people during a landmark inquiry. He says that 29 years later, it's time for action.

items.title: Property market correction visible as auction clearance rates drop
items.description: Early signs of an Australian housing market correction are now clearly visible, and at the heart of the recent property market weakness is less vendor power.

items.title: 'Catastrophic failure' after drones malfunction at Vivid Sydney show
items.description: The incident occurred not long into Monday's 7.30pm "star-bound" show when almost 90 drones began falling out of formation and into the harbour around Cockle Bay.

items.title: One world record and a whole lot of regret for Enhanced Games athletes
items.description: Despite the drugs and the super suits, the Enhanced Games delivered little more than a smattering of PBs and a single world fastest time for the hefty price of an athlete's hard-earned credibility.

items.title: Breaking: Brad Scott sacked as Essendon coach
items.description: Essendon sacks head coach Brad Scott as the Bombers languish at the bottom of the AFL ladder.

items.title: 'My time to go': The words that showed Daniher's humanity in tragedy
items.description: Neale Daniher showed leadership on and off the field throughout his life, from club captaincy to coaching and as Australian of the Year — but no more so when facing the challenge of an MND diagnosis.

items.title: Richard Gadd 'couldn't escape' the story he wanted to tell after Baby Reindeer
items.description: After Baby Reindeer — about a comedian and his stalker — became a surprise hit, Richard Gadd ignored the pressure to replicate his success, making the show he couldn't stop thinking about.

items.title: Using AI to manage your budget? This is what experts want you to know
items.description: "Hallucinations", privacy and other factors to consider if you’re turning to artificial intelligence financial advice.

items.title: Flag quiz: Which country has the most purple on its flag?
items.description: What's the name of the solo star on the Australian flag? And can you tell the difference between the Russian and Dutch flags?

items.title: Pope Leo warns of AI becoming 'yet another Tower of Babel'
items.description: Pope Leo XIV urges global governments to slow down the development of AI systems and their disruptive effects.

items.title: NACC chief Brereton to face Senate grilling after shock resignation
items.description: National Anti-Corruption Commissioner Paul Brereton will face a grilling by senators at estimates hearings today following his shock resignation on Monday, amid calls for a wider reset of the troubled agency.

items.title: 'No quick fix' for social housing squatters taking over Sydney units
items.description: Social housing tenants in inner Sydney have repeatedly complained about illegal squatters, they have been removed by police but they keep coming back.

items.title: Live: Oil falls on peace deal hopes and ASX set to rise
items.description: The oil price has fallen 7 per cent on hopes the conflict in Iran will end in a peace deal. Follow the day's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: Ebola outbreak outpacing health response, WHO chief says
items.description: It comes as health facilities in some of the worst-hit regions are attacked amid ongoing violence.

items.title: Flexible work broader than just working from home
items.description: A bill amending the Fair Work Act 2009 to include the right to work from home is too narrow in its focus and could lead to discrimination, according to submissions in a federal inquiry.

items.title: Australian family demands action one year after son's Bali death
items.description: A year after their 23-year-old son died in Bali in "unclear" circumstances, a Queensland couple have unanswered questions.

items.title: Community 'devastated' by plans for gas-powered data centres
items.description: More than 200 people voice their opposition to plans to build one of the country’s largest gas-fired power plants in the NSW Southern Highlands to provide energy for data centres.
